content:
jess (support): FYI customer reported erratic embeddings behavior this morning. They expect 768-dim vectors but intermittently get 1536 and the embeddings endpoint spikes tail latency when batch sizes go above ~64. Attached logs from their reproducer.

maria (support): thanks — can you paste the minimal repro (curl or SDK) and pm the customer id? also which model alias are they calling?

jess (support): repro snippet they used: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-small:latest","input":["what is LLM inference?","tokenization details..."]}'
```
Customer id: cust-42. They said the SDK uses dynamic batching and they set max_batch_size=128.

tom (eng-runtime): interesting. log tail shows multiple batch assembly events where grouping_key is not set and we see mixed model ids being merged into the same batch. snippet from runtime logs: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] batching_assemble id=pool-7 size=72 group_key=null model_variants=[embed-small,embed-large] assembled_dims=1536
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] dispatch batch_id=xyz latency=980ms tokens=...
```
This would cause the per-batch post-processing to assume a single embedding dimension and fail for smaller-model requests, resulting in dim mismatch and expensive fallback that spikes tail latency.

lev (eng-ml): to be clear, embed-small -> 768, embed-large -> 1536. If dynamic batching merges them we can either: 1) enforce grouping by model alias, 2) reject mixes at assembly time (fast fail), or 3) have transparent upcasting (not desirable). Which option is least disruptive?

maria (support): customer currently on Dedicated trial; we disabled dynamic batching for cust-42 as a stopgap. They now get stable dims but throughput lower. Need permanent fix and a repro we can run on staging.

sre-oliver (eng-sre): I pushed a temporary guard on staging that rejects mixed-model batches and returns a 409 with reason "mixed_model_variants_in_batch". That avoided the dim errors in our runs. Suggest we add grouping by model to SDK examples and console defaults.

tom (eng-runtime): root cause theory: routing policy allowed model alias fallback/compat routing to pick embed-large when embed-small capacity was low; dynamic batcher didn't include model variant in the grouping key. Fix: include "model_alias" in batch grouping key and add a config flag batching.reject_mixed_variants=true by default for embeddings. I'll open a PR.

maria (support): can we get a minimal repro command we can hand the customer that demonstrates the bug and the mitigation? Prefer a short script that toggles max_batch_size and shows the error vs success.

lev (eng-ml): repro script (quick): ```python
# toggles batch size and model header to provoke mixed batch
import requests, time
URL='https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
KEY='staging-key'
headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {KEY}','Content-Type':'application/json'}
def call(model, n):
  payload={'model': model, 'input':['x']*n}
  return requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=headers).status_code, requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=headers).text
# simulate many concurrent small calls to trigger dynamic batching
for _ in range(20):
  # alternate models to hit the bug
  call('embed-small:latest',1)
  call('embed-large:latest',1)
  time.sleep(0.02)
```
This should reproduce mixed batches on staging if dynamic batching is enabled and max_batch_size high.

maria (support): perfect. I'll send this to cust-42 and advise lowering max_batch_size to 32 or disabling dynamic batching while we deploy the fix. Also we'll suggest pinning model variant in the request header to avoid fallback routing.

sre-oliver (eng-sre): operational notes: added a tracing tag "batching.group_key" to batch spans and an alert when batching_assemble.group_key==null and assembled_size>48. Alerting rule in #eng-sre.

tom (eng-runtime): PR opened: add model_alias to default grouping_key + config toggle to reject mixed variants. Will add unit test that simulates concurrent requests and asserts no mixed batches assembled.

maria (support): follow-ups: 1) tell customer to set max_batch_size=32 and group_by=model in SDK; 2) we'll schedule a maintenance window to roll the guard to prod tomorrow; 3) update docs with example and FAQ.

jess (support): customer notified, they accepted the workaround for now. leaving thread open until deploy-bot shows prod rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: staging->prod (batching-group-key-fix) 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z. CI: ✅, canary: running.

deploy-bot: Canary passed. Rolling to prod.

tom (eng-runtime): prod rollout complete. Guard enabled and grouping_key default changed. We also added a soft limit warning in console when route-config max_batch_size > 64 for embeddings.

maria (support): closing after customer confirms stable results tomorrow. Thanks team :tada:
